rank_math_title: 3 Day Okavango Delta Mokoro Safari from Maun
rank_math_desc: 3 day Okavango Delta mokoro safari from Maun: 2 nights island bush camping, guided walks and sunset mokoro trips. From USD 715 per adult.
post_content: This 3 day Okavango Delta mokoro safari takes you from Maun by traditional dugout canoe to a remote island bush camp for 2 nights of guided walks, poling lessons and sunsets on the water.
overview:
This 3 day Okavango Delta mokoro safari is a 3-day, 2-night canoe and walking trip from Maun into the heart of Botswana's Okavango Delta. You glide by traditional mokoro to a remote island, sleep 2 nights in a bush camp, and spend the days on guided walks, poling lessons and sunset trips on the water. The price starts from USD 715 per adult, and it suits active travellers who want a quiet, back-to-nature Delta adventure.

The trip runs on full board with camping equipment, bed linen and towels supplied, and a Divulge Adventures representative handles the road transfer from Maun to the mokoro station and back.

Why choose a 3 day Okavango Delta mokoro safari?

The mokoro is a dugout canoe pushed along by a standing poler, so you travel through the Delta's reed channels and lagoons with no engine noise at all. That silence lets you hear birds, frogs and moving wildlife, and it brings you down to water level for photos you cannot take from a vehicle.

Island bush camping means you sleep inside the wilderness rather than in a lodge on its edge. Walks with your guide focus on tracks, plants and the smaller details of the ecosystem, which makes this a very different experience from a classic game-drive safari.

  • Nature lovers: silent mokoro trips and guided island walks every day.
  • Short on time: a real Okavango experience in 3 days from Maun.
  • Budget-minded travellers: a bush camp keeps the cost well below fly-in lodges.

What to expect on the 3 day Okavango Delta mokoro safari

Day 1 starts with a morning pick-up in Maun and a road transfer to the mokoro station, where you meet your poler. After about 1 to 2 hours on the water you reach a remote island, set up at the bush camp and head out on a guided nature walk. Dinner is served around the campfire.

Day 2 begins with an early walk in the cool hours, the best time to track animals. After brunch and a rest, you try seasonal catch-and-release fishing, learn to pole a mokoro yourself, then take an afternoon mokoro excursion with a short walk and a sundowner on the water.

Day 3 opens with a final early-morning walk and breakfast. You then pack up, glide back through the reeds and lagoons to the mokoro station, and transfer by road to Maun, where the safari ends.

When is the best time for a mokoro safari?

The Okavango Delta's floodwaters usually peak in the dry winter months, roughly June to August, which is when the channels are fullest for mokoro trips and wildlife gathers near the water. Water levels change each year, so we confirm conditions when you book. Read our best time to visit Botswana guide for a month-by-month view.

What is included in the Okavango mokoro trip?

The price includes park fees for non-residents, all activities unless marked optional, 2 nights of bush camp accommodation, camping equipment, bed linen and bath towels, a professional guide and poler, all transport, round-trip transfers, meals, drinks and all taxes and VAT.

Not included are international flights, extra accommodation before or after the tour, tips, personal items, any government increases in taxes or park fees, and some meals. See how this trip fits a wider itinerary in our Okavango Delta safari guide and our Botswana safari guide. For more time in the region, see the 5 Days Into the Okavango Exploration trip.

From USD 715 per adult. The final price depends on your travel dates, group size and the camps available, and we confirm every detail in your written quote.

faq.q: When is the best time for the 3 day Okavango Delta mokoro safari?
faq.a: The 3 day Okavango Delta mokoro safari runs best when the floodwaters are high, usually from about June to August, because the channels are full and animals stay close to the water. Water levels vary from year to year, so we check conditions for your dates before confirming the mokoro trip.

faq.q: What is included in the 3 day Okavango Delta mokoro safari?
faq.a: The 3 day Okavango Delta mokoro safari includes non-resident park fees, all listed activities, 2 nights of bush camp accommodation, camping equipment, bed linen and towels, a professional guide and poler, transport and transfers from Maun, meals, drinks and taxes. International flights, extra nights, tips and personal items are not included.

faq.q: Where do you stay on the Okavango Delta mokoro safari?
faq.a: On the Okavango Delta mokoro safari you stay 2 nights in a bush camp set up on a remote island inside the Delta, reached by mokoro from the mokoro station. Camping equipment, bed linen and bath towels are provided, and dinners are served around the campfire. There is no lodge on this trip.

faq.q: How fit do you need to be for the Okavango mokoro trip?
faq.a: The Okavango mokoro trip suits anyone with average fitness who is happy to sit in a low canoe for 1 to 2 hours and walk at a gentle pace on uneven ground. Walks start early to avoid the heat. Families with older children can join, and we advise on minimum ages when you enquire.
